core_obligations: Quote exactness at the left of the sequence and statement (2) from the closure lemma (proof lines 1012-1013).
Build the canonical map c : M^/N^ -> (M/N)^ from the composite M^ -> (M/N)^ (proof lines 1013-1015).
Show M^/N^ is complete and M^ -> M^/N^ is open, by the quotient lemma (proof lines 1015-1017).
Apply the universal property of completion to obtain b : (M/N)^ -> M^/N^ (proof lines 1017-1019).
Conclude that b and c are mutually inverse since they agree on a dense subset, which gives exactness at the right and openness (proof lines 1019-1022).
proof_roadmap: Exactness at the left and the description of N^ (proof lines 1012-1013).
The round trip through the completion of the quotient (proof lines 1013-1019).
Mutually inverse maps by density (proof lines 1019-1022).
difficulty_reason: For a linearly topologized module M over a topological ring R with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0 and a submodule N, the lemma asserts that the induced sequence of completions 0 -> N^ -> M^ -> (M/N)^ -> 0 is exact, that N^ is the closure of the image of N in M^, and that M^ -> (M/N)^ is open (statement lines 997-1010). The proof is displayed in full: exactness at the left and statement (2) are quoted from the closure lemma, the canonical map c : M^/N^ -> (M/N)^ is produced, completeness of M^/N^ and openness of M^ -> M^/N^ come from the quotient lemma, the universal property of completion yields the inverse map b, and b and c are mutually inverse because they agree on a dense subset (proof lines 1012-1022). The level is H2: the whole zig-zag of canonical maps is constructed and checked, no step is omitted.
